desk.headline: Gold income up 8% to $2.6bn on higher prices but output down 9% and headline EPS $1.55 missed; production guidance reaffirmed

numbers.eps_basis: headline earnings per share (155 US cents)

results: Gold income rose 8% to $2.6bn as the price received climbed 21% to $4,239/oz, more than offsetting a 9% fall in output to 696koz.
Headline earnings rose to $790m (155 US cents a share) from $672m, below the 170-cent estimate.
Costs rose sharply: all-in sustaining cost was $2,170/oz (+26%) and total cash cost $1,534/oz (+25%), with gold-linked royalties and fuel prices cited.
Iduapriem (-43%), Obuasi (-26%), Sukari (-21%) and Tropicana (-15%) produced less, while Siguiri rose 49%.
Free cash flow fell to $722m on higher capex ($563m), taxes and working capital; net cash rose to $1.26bn and a 71 US cent dividend was declared.

guidance.summary: AngloGold kept its 2026 gold production guidance of 2.80–3.17Moz and expects a stronger fourth quarter. The release does not restate cost or capex guidance.

items.metric: Growth capex at Geita, Siguiri and Cuiabá

points: Management put the Q3 output drop down to planned grade sequencing in open pits and short-term problems it says have since normalised.
Q4 should recover: Iduapriem has been dewatered after flooding, Sukari stripping is opening higher-grade ore and Obuasi is ramping up again after a fatality.
Most of the cost rise was blamed on outside factors such as gold-price-linked royalties and higher fuel costs.
The board approved funding for the North Bullfrog project in Nevada, subject to permits; the Arthur feasibility study is on schedule.
Two safety incidents were noted: fatalities at Obuasi earlier in the year and at Sukari in August.
call.source: Company results release commentary and coverage: Business Day, 5 Nov 2026

watch: Whether Q4 output recovers enough to land within the 2.80–3.17Moz range.
Cost per ounce as royalties and fuel costs track gold and oil prices.
Permitting and spending on North Bullfrog and the Nevada projects.
